dialogOption.texten: 911, what's your emergency?
My wife is giving birth!
{WHERE?} Sir, keep calm. Where are you?
{ANY CONTRACTIONS?} Is your wife having contractions?

dialogOption.emotions: [horns], very nervous, almost begging for help
dialogOption.texten: We were heading to hospital, but we get stuck in a traffic jam! There is no way we can get out of here! Please help us!
Yes... wait a second . . do you have contractions? . . . . . . . . . . . . Contractions are getting stronger and occur very often. Send an ambulance quickly!
{WHAT MONTH IS IT?} How far along is your wife's pregnancy?

dialogOption.emotions: [horns], very nervous, almost begging for help
dialogOption.texten: She's in her ninth month, sir! We need help!
{WHERE ARE YOU?} Sir, do you know where you are, can you give me address?
We're stuck near [[ADDRESS]].
We're stuck near 20 Frote Road
We're stuck near 104 9th Alley
We're stuck near 154 Downtown Street
{YOU HAVE TO ACT} Sir, I've sent an ambulance, but it may not arrive before the baby does.

dialogOption.emotions: panically [background at the end until player choose operator line: mumbling: Oh my god... what now... I can't... ]
dialogOption.texten: What?! What does it mean?! That's our baby!!! I don't know what to do!!!

dialogOption.texten: {BE A MAN} Hey, sir! You need to be strong, strong for your wife, strong for your baby. And believe me when I say this your wife has far tougher job ahead of her, ok?
{EVERYTHING WILL BE FINE} Everything's gonna be fine, sir. Do you have a name for the baby yet?
Em... yes. We're expecting a girl, so we'll name her Lucy, after my grandma.
{STAY CALM} That's a beautiful name. So, please be calm, listen my instructions and together we will take care of your wife and Lucy, sound good?

dialogOption.emotions: [deep breath] definitely more calm than before
dialogOption.texten: . . . . . okay... let's do it...
I-I'll try...
What should I do first?
{TAKE OFF HER CLOTHES} What you're gonna have to do is expose your wife from waist down. So you're gonna help take her pants off. She shouldn't have anything below the waist.
{LAY HER DOWN} I want you to get your wife comfortable on a back on a steady flat surface.
{FIND SOMEONE TO HELP} I want you to get out of your car and see if you can find someone else also stuck in traffic, who maybe is a medical professional.
Should I leave my wife alone?!
{NO} No, that's a bad idea.
Then what should I do???
{YES} Yes. Try to do it quickly.
Okay... So... I'm going. Thanks for the help... I guess...
Okay, wait. I'll make some space on the backseat . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
Thank God I bought a big car. . . . . . . . .
Lay down, honey. You need to lay down. . . . . . . . . . . . .
Okay, what's next?

dialogOption.emotions: to his wife [sound of taking off clothes]
dialogOption.texten: Honey, you need to take off your pants... Let me help you . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
{RELAX AND WAIT} Now, your wife should try to relax and breath deeply. She'll probably have an urge to push very soon.
{WATER BREAKING?} Has her water broken?
My wife says so...
{PUSH} Now, you should tell your wife to push.
Push, honey! Push! Come on!
Relax, sweetheart. Take a deep breaths. Yes, like that. Everything will be okay.
I see the baby!
{CAN YOU SEE THE HEAD?} Can you see the head?
I can't! I don't see the head! Oh God, those are legs. Christ, what I'm supposed to do?!
Your wife needs to stop pushing or at least delay her labor. The ambulance is on the way.
{PULL OUT THE BABY} You should pull the baby in your direction.
Yes, it's the head!
What? I can't do that! The head is slippery and I don't want to hurt the baby.
{WAIT} Okay, wait until the baby is out. You'll need to catch her and protect her from falling.
Okay, okay. Darling, you can do this!
Oh, my God...... she's here. It's a girl! Our baby...
{CONGRATS!} Congratulations! You did it!
Thank you!
{IS IT BREATHING?} Is Lucy breathing? Is she crying?

dialogOption.emotions: extremly happy, crying a bit [child starts crying]
dialogOption.texten: Yes, she is... she looks healthy and beautiful. My sweet Lucy...
She isn't crying! I don't know... I don't know if she's breathing!
{RUB HER BACK} Don't panic, sir. If she's not crying you may need to clear her airway. Use your little finger to remove any mucus from her mouth, then turn her over, face down, and pat her back.
{WAIT FOR HELP} Don't do anything, just wait for an ambulance. It's on the way.

dialogOption.emotions: extremly happy, crying a bit [child starts crying]
dialogOption.texten: Okay. . . . . It worked! Oh, Jesus, I'm so happy, Lucy is alive!
{GIVE CHILD TO YOUR WIFE} You can give Lucy to your wife.
{PUT CHILD ON MOTHER'S STOMACH} You should put the child on mother's stomach.
Sure...... Oh, I can't do it, because of umbilical cord. Sweet God, I almost disrupted it.
{TIE THE CORD} Find something to tie the umbilical cord. It could be anything: ribbon, string or even a clean shoelace.
dialogOption.COMMENT: mistake was caller insted of operator

dialogOption.texten: {IS IT PULSATING?} Check if the umbilical cord is still pulsating.
No, it isn't!
Okay, I got a ribbon.
{MAKE A KNOT} Now, you should make a knot about 1,5 inches from the newborn's belly.
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . It's done. Should I cut it?
{DO IT} Yes, do it immediately.
{NOT NECESSARILY} It isn't necessary. You can wait with that until you get to the hospital.
Okay... The traffic jam looks a bit smaller. Should I drive to the hospital or an ambulance will arrive here?
{WAIT} Just wait, the ambulance is almost there.
{DRIVE ON YOUR OWN} The hardest part is behind you and your wife too. Drive her to the hospital and drive carefully.
Okay, thank you very much sir.
Oh God, we'll try. Please, hurry!
So what should I do now?

reportElement.texten: A pregnant woman started giving a birth in a traffic jam.
The operator gave wrong medical instruction.
The operator succesfully calmed the man down.
The operator didn't manage to calm down the man.
The operator put the woman in danger. Her husband left her alone, because of the operator's instruction.
The operator didn't give important medical instruction, which put the newborn's life in danger.
